newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian average lending rate back up to 11 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian average lending rate back up to 11 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate rose 20 bps again to 11 percent on Friday amid stronger demand for kuna due to pension payments, dealers said.
They put total settlements at 38.6 million kuna, of which 37 were new bank borrowings.
Call money loans were made at 10.5 percent. Term rates ranged between 11 percent for shorters three-day interbank loans and 16 percent for one-month funds for savings banks.
Insurers charged a steady nine percent for renewed one-week deals and 13 percent for one month.

The central bank calculated the kuna midrates weaker at 5.9338 versus 5.8865 to the dollar and at 3.5694 to the German mark. These rates are for Saturday and next Monday dealings. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
